record.requirement: An app declares nodes inside a canvas with an author key, role, name and region, and the driver treats them as elements across the snapshot, diff, click, refusals, UI graph, actions, coverage, layout and exploration; Circle Drawer's circles are virtual nodes
record.observed_gap: A snapshot node needs an author id and a DOM element, so an agent sees a canvas as one opaque element; the UI graph reserves no id form for a non-DOM node; the layout verb reserves an app-canvas placing and the widget trait a commented accessibility tree.

body:
# Forks — 2026-11-26-canvas-keyboard-path (Canvas keyboard path)

Written at phase P4 on the operator's take-up direction (inputs#I1): every fork the plan meets other than F1 B1, which
the founder answered himself (inputs#I2, «B1: выделение полем») and which is not re-opened here. For each fork: what
crosses, the rule it meets, each option's measured cost, its dependences, whose it is and the most conservative option
that still builds the entry. Default: none — nothing below is taken until the operator relays the answers.

Run dir: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-26T06-28-33-phase/` · scope `doc:2026-11-26-canvas-keyboard-path/scope` rev 3 ·
research rev 1 · HEAD `255a586fb`.

**Founder forks found: yes — F1 B and F1 C each change the tree's focus or active-descendant contract for every Dioxus
document behind `custom-widget`, and F1 C also reaches past his «Оставить записанным» on the active descendant.** F1 A
and every option of F2–F5 are the operator's. F1 A builds the entry with no founder word beyond B1.

**Standing beside every option: B1 itself** (the founder's word). `VirtualNodeDeclaration` gains `selected`:
`custom_widget.rs` +1 field and doc line; `dioxus_document.rs` +2 lines (`set_selected` beside `set_disabled`, :416);
`snapshot.rs` +1 line (the virtual branch reads `selected: tree_node.is_selected()`, :183); the 4 declaration literals
in 4 files take `selected: false` (re-derived: `git grep -n "VirtualNodeDeclaration {" -- packages tests examples`, 5
hits, 1 the definition; the prior forks file's 8 was at `a5d18f604`). The app: a selection signal with its declared
writes, a click inside a circle selecting it and adding none, the selected circle painted filled.

How costs were measured: file and line reads at HEAD `255a586fb`; name greps (each command named beside its count);
the rows files and histories of the run dir. No code-graph query ran (research is `derived-without-graph`). A cost
marked *derived* is read from source or CSS, not from a run.

Terms searched across all seven masters (`rec.py find --root . --doc all --text …`): `active descendant` (6 rows),
`tree's focus` (8), `accessibility-tree/focus` (2), `virtual node reads` (5), `keyboard-virtual-nodes` (1).

---

## F1 — How the engine, the tree and the snapshot name the current circle

**Today.** The tree's focus is `focus_node_id` filtered to the built nodes, else the window
(`accessibility.rs:105-110`). The virtual nodes are appended afterwards in dioxus-native-dom
(`dioxus_document.rs:400-420`), which never sets `tree.focus`. The snapshot reads `focused` as `id == tree.focus`
(`snapshot.rs:122`, `:183`). The stand's shared reader `focused` (`tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs`) asserts that
the snapshot's focused ids equal the tree's focus. The canvas carries no `tabindex` and no key handler
(`circle_drawer.rs:310-352`).

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Under every option the canvas becomes a Tab stop and its key handler is the app's
own: a focused canvas is outside the engine's Enter and Space arms (security-plan
`decision/enter-activates-focused-control`). Under B the adapter and the snapshot get a focus on a node with no element.
Under C they get an engine-written active descendant and a `highlighted` reading on a virtual node. Both are closed
values inside the ratified carriers (security-plan `decision/boundary-widening-rule`), but each changes a ratified
engine contract.

| Option | What it does | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | One Tab stop, as the CRUD list and Cells' grid: `circle-canvas` takes `tabindex: "0"` and an app `onkeydown`; the current circle is the selected one (B1's `selected`); the engine, the tree and the snapshot all read focus on `circle-canvas` | App only (`circle_drawer.rs`, the `cells.rs:414-436` form); no engine or dioxus-native-dom line beyond B1. Rows: a11y `absence/keyboard-virtual-nodes` retired; a11y `decision/stated-tab-order-walked` gains Circle Drawer. An assistive technology learns the current circle from `selected` alone — the CRUD list's stated limit (a11y `decision/active-descendant-unread`) |
| B | The tree's focus names the selected circle's virtual node while the engine holds the canvas; the snapshot follows the tree | `dioxus_document.rs` *derived* ~6–10 lines (after the loop at :400-420, `tree.focus` set to the selected node's tree id where `focus_node_id` is the canvas); `snapshot.rs` none; the shared `focused` reader and `stand_keyboard`'s three-way agreement re-stated, because the engine's focus is then the canvas while the tree's is the circle. Rows amended: architecture and a11y-plan `contract/accessibility-tree/focus`, security-plan `decision/accessibility-focus-built-nodes-only`, architecture `contract/snapshot/virtual-node` (focused), a11y-plan `decision/stated-tab-order-walked` (what «agree» means), architecture `decision/hit-focus-form-engine-changes` (its tally) |
| C | The canvas names the selected circle as its active descendant, engine-written as the open select list's is (`accessibility.rs:232-240`); the tree's focus stays on the canvas; the snapshot reads that circle `highlighted` | `dioxus_document.rs` *derived* ~3–5 lines (`set_active_descendant` on the canvas node); `snapshot.rs`, the `highlighted` set taking virtual ids. Rows amended: architecture `contract/accessibility-tree/active-descendant` and `contract/node-keys/highlighted` (an open select's row alone today), a11y-plan `contract/snapshot/open-list-highlighted-row`, design-system `contract/select-accessibility/open-select`. It reaches past a11y-plan `decision/active-descendant-unread` and `decision/active-descendant-kept-unread` (the founder's F2 «Оставить записанным», 2026-10-14, F3 B 2026-10-18), though no page `aria-activedescendant` is read |

**Dependences.** F2 (the keys that move the selection). B1 is the current-circle state under every option. Under B a
selection change must also mark the changed set, or a windowed adapter never hears the focus move (architecture
`decision/declaration-change-marks-nothing` would be amended).

**Whose.** A — the operator's (an app change; the security history: «the Circle Drawer canvas taking a Tab stop and a
key handler that moves a current circle follows the same app-level shape», the Cells precedent ratified on the founder's
F13). B — the founder's: «Making a virtual node the tree's focus is an engine change for every document behind the
feature, so it goes to the founder» (security-plan history, 2026-10-31-engine-debts). C — the founder's: it reaches
past his recorded word on the active descendant.

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A. The entry asks that the engine, the snapshot and the tree agree, and
under A they agree on `circle-canvas` at every step.

---

## F2 — The keys on the focused canvas, and what acts on the current circle

**Today.** The diameter dialog opens only by a double click on the nearest circle (`circle_drawer.rs:339-358`). The
driver's `press` takes 12 key names (`schema.rs:22-35`: tab, enter, escape, backspace, delete, space, the four arrows,
home, end) and acts on what holds focus (`execute.rs:292`).

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Nothing new: `press` keys are already call content in a kept check (security-plan
`decision/kept-check-call-content`). Under F1 A the app's key handler must be the actor (security-plan history
2026-10-13).

| Option | Keys | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | The four arrows move the selection to the previous or next circle in declared order, clamped, the first arrow with none selected selecting the first; Enter opens the diameter dialog on the selected circle | App only; `stand_keyboard` rows for Circle Drawer; the canvas `onkeydown` joins the UI graph's handlers and the coverage tables (`HANDLERS_AT_BOOT`, `UNEXERCISED_AFTER_DRIVES`); per the Cells history (amd-dbogce46) a key handler may move `stand_non_lean_tasks`' counts |
| B | A, plus Home and End to the first and last circle, and Escape clearing the selection | as A, +3 match arms and their rows |

**Dependences.** F1 (under B or C the same keys also move the tree's focus or active descendant). B1: a selection
change repaints a fill, so each move changes the canvas answer's lines.

**Whose.** The operator's (app behaviour, no crossing).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A.

**A side question in the same class: does a pointer click on a circle focus the canvas?** Today it does not: a click
on a custom-widget target runs no click walk and clears no focus (architecture `decision/widget-click-synthesis`). A —
unchanged (a mouse user then Tabs to the canvas before the keys act). B — the app's `onclick` calls `set_focus` through
its `MountedData` handle (the buffered render, architecture `decision/dioxus-bridge-buffered-render`), so the keys act
after a click, the focus events firing. The operator's; most conservative: A.

---

## F3 — `covered` on the stand (the prior chunk's F4, open as CARRY `cry-yr2aexmx` states)

**Today.** A virtual node reads `covered` only by an element over its region's centre (F12 A, delegate, PROVISIONAL:
architecture and security-plan `contract/refusal-causes/covered`, a11y-plan `contract/driver-click-refusals/covered`,
test-plan `contract/refusal-cause/covered`). The stand has no such element: the dialog `.cd-dialog` lies in flow below
the canvas (`circle_drawer.rs:447-458`, `margin-top: 16px`), never over it. `stand_circle_nodes.rs:348`
`a_circle_under_another_is_not_refused_covered` pins it.

**What crosses / the rule it meets.** Nothing new crosses (a closed cause word). The meaning text of `covered` is one of
the eight fixed texts (ratified 2026-10-18); a clause was added to it once with its name, remedy and order unmoved
(test-plan `amd-4g5qmthy`).

| Option | What it does | Measured / derived cost |
|---|---|---|
| A | Kept: elements alone cover. Under B1 a click on a circle under another selects the top one, so the diff names the top circle, not the one named | 0 code; the stand witness re-read under B1 (the diff names `c2`); v040-11's «covered … refused with that cause» is not read on the stand |
| B | A later-declared taken node of the same canvas whose region holds the target's centre covers it | `execute.rs` `covered` (one function, shared with `actions` through `check_target`); the four covered rows above take one clause; measured by the prior forks file on its fixture sequence: 2 of 12 circles and 26 of 100 read `covered`; on the stand every centre click stacks at (348,198), so all but the last of N circles read `covered` |
| C | The app draws its dialog over the canvas (absolute position), so the dialog's element covers the circles under it | `circle_drawer.rs` CSS; the dialog's layout pins move (`stand_lint`, `stand_contrast` if it reads the dialog, the snapshot bounds); no rule changes |

**Dependences.** B1 (without B, a click on a covered circle selects the top one). F4 and F5: v040-11's claim needs all
three stand readings.

**Whose.** The operator's (the rows B changes are a delegate's PROVISIONAL; the cause's name, remedy and order are
unmoved). C — the operator's (an app layout change).

**Most conservative that builds the entry:** A (the entry does not name `covered`).

---

## F4 — `disabled` on the stand

**Today.** Every circle is declared `disabled: false` (`circle_drawer.rs:230`). A virtual node reads `enabled` from its
declaration (architecture `contract/snapshot/virtual-node`, a11y-plan `contract/snapshot/enabled`).

| B | While the diameter dialog is open, every circle but the one it adjusts is declared disabled | App: the widget reads one more attribute (for example `data-adjusting`, leaving the founder-ratified `data-circles` form `x,y,d,id` of layout-templates `decision/circle-drawer-circles-painted-on-canvas` unmoved); a stand check; the snapshot's `enabled` on circles moves while the dialog is open |

**Whose.** The operator's (app behaviour; `disabled` is a closed reading in a ratified carrier).

## F5 — `off-screen` on the stand
